title: Zenith on-prem triage + install deep-dive (weekly)
content:
Weekly triage notes for Zenith (on-prem) install — focused deep-dive on recurring failures seen during weeks 2–3 of the pilot. Goal: consolidate hypotheses, short-term mitigations, and mid-term product fixes to avoid repeated hands-on field support.

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Kai Patel (installer), Riley Brooks (SRE), Sofia Alvarez (security/keys), Jamal Reed (solutions eng), Zenith engineering reps (remote).

Background / summary of observed failure modes (recurring):
- Installer appears to finish, but runtime services fail to reach steady-state on ~30% of nodes after the final configuration step. Services crash with gRPC errors and frequent TLS handshake failures when connecting to KMS and internal control-plane endpoints.
- Intermittent GPU initialization failures on one older host type in the customer's rack (driver inverse-mismatch: host reports NVIDIA 530.18 but container libs expect 535.x).
- Large, sporadic increase in tokenization latency correlated with network retransmits between nodes (observed in tcpdump).
- NTP drift on one zone leading to cert validation errors on >24h windows.

Primary hypotheses (ranked):
1) MTU/path MTU blackhole and jumbo frames: Zenith’s switching fabric uses intermittent jumbo-frame segments; when packets exceed 1500 and get silently dropped, TLS handshakes and gRPC larger frames are dropped, causing many retries and eventual service crash.
2) KMS integration race + expired local TLS cache: the installer writes KMS certs early but the runtime's KMS client opens connections before the KMS node is fully reachable; race causes initial handshake failures that persist because we cache a failure state.
3) Driver/OCI runtime mismatch for GPUs on legacy hosts: installer did not enforce a strict driver-version gating for older SKUs; container GPU libraries try to access missing symbols and OOM or segfault.
4) Time skew: nodes with >120s drift fail cert pin checks sporadically, causing service restarts.

Evidence collected this week:
- tcpdump from node-17 (Zenith) shows large ICMP fragmentation-needed responses suppressed by firewall, but we see retransmit bursts during TLS handshake.
- dmesg from host shows nvidia-modeset: unresolved symbol for nvidia_uvm on boot for host-type B.
- installer logs: installer/step-07-kms shows 503 and TLS alert records 50s into final validate loop; retried 6 times then marked node unhealthy.
- NTP logs: chrony drift register on a cluster of nodes connected to an older stratum-1 appliance with intermittent GPS lock.

Immediate mitigations (apply in next 48 hours):
- On-call playbook change: add MTU sanity check to preflight that tries an MTU 9000 probe and falls back; if PMTU blackhole suspected, set install to static 1500 until network team confirms jumbo support. Owner: Kai. ETA: 2026-08-07.
- KMS client: add fast-retry with exponential backoff + clear TLS connection cache on transient handshake errors (temporary fix in agent launch script) so initial race doesn't persist. Owner: Sofia. Patch: installer agent hotfix branch. ETA: 2026-08-06.
- GPU gating: add host SKU detection (via lshw) and block installer from enabling container GPU hooks if driver < 535; instruct field to upgrade driver or schedule node replacement. Owner: Jamal. ETA: 2026-08-08 for blocker check, 2026-08-20 for fully automated gating.
- NTP: change chrony config to use multiple strata and enable local fallback; provide customers checklist to replace aging GPS appliance. Owner: Riley. ETA: 2026-08-07.

Mid-term product fixes (design work to start immediately):
- Installer preflight extension: add network probe suite (MTU/probe, DNS path, TLS handshake simulation, gRPC small/large frame test) with >=3s per test and explicit failure categories written to preflight-report.json. This will help us decide whether to retry with conservative defaults or require operator remediation. Designer: Kai + Riley. Spec draft due: 2026-08-14.
- KMS integration hardened client library: implement a handshake-state machine that persists successful root CA and rotation metadata but never persists permanent failures — instead mark as "transient" for N retries and expose diagnostic page with last-5-handshake-errors. Owner: Sofia. RFC due: 2026-08-18.
- GPU compatibility matrix in installer and console: surface supported host driver ranges per model variant; block incompatible pairings during plan creation. Owner: Jamal. Design doc due: 2026-08-21.
- Telemetry: add short-lived gRPC/TLS failure counters in the agent that are shipped to the console for private deployment customers (opt-in). This will allow preemptive alerts from our SRE team when patterns match known failure signatures. Owner: Riley. PoC: 2026-08-28.

Action items (tracked):
- Kai: commit preflight MTU probe and fail-safe fallback (PR #352 referenced). Due: 2026-08-07.
- Sofia: push temporary TLS cache-clear hotfix and run to Zenith nodes with consent. Due: 2026-08-06.
- Jamal: deliver host SKU detection script and one-off remediation runbook. Due: 2026-08-08.
- Riley: update chrony template and coordinate with Zenith infra for appliance swap. Due: 2026-08-07.
- Maya: coordinate weekly status email to Zenith execs and schedule deep-dive call Thursday 2026-08-06 10:00 PT. Due: 2026-08-05 (email draft in Slack).

Risks and open questions:
- Zenith policy prohibits rebooting >2 nodes during business hours. Some of our remediations require reboots to load updated drivers — need approval window.
- Telemetry opt-in: legal/privacy sign-off may take multiple weeks; need interim remote-run diagnostic bundle.
- If MTU blackhole is intermittent, our preflight could pass, then production fail. We proposed adding a continuous MTU health check post-install (agent-level lightweight probe) — but this increases telemetry surface.

Notes from customer: Zenith provided a switch log showing a firmware upgrade coincident with onset of issues (firmware 3.2.4 -> 3.3.0). They will schedule a rollback window if we can demonstrate the correlation. Zenith engineering also provided a list of host-serials for the legacy SKU cluster; they've agreed to maintenance window for replacement of 6 nodes next week.

Next sync: deep-dive Thursday 2026-08-06 10:00 PT. Agenda: review MTU probe PR feedback, confirm hotfix rollout plan, finalize driver gating approach, and confirm maintenance window dates with Zenith.

Appendix (diagnostics collected):
- excerpts: installer logs (step-07-kms) 2026-08-04 14:33:12: "TLS alert unexpected_message" repeated 4x then 503.
- tcpdump snippet: TLS client hello size 1720 bytes followed by no server response for 30s then retransmit; subsequent server ICMP frag-needed observed on the network trace.
- dmesg snippet: "nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required symbol missing - nvidia_uvm: unresolved symbol" on host-type B.

If anything here is unclear, call out before the Thursday sync. This doc will be updated with roll-forward notes after each mitigation is exercised on Zenith test nodes.

-- Maya C., eng-private-deployments
